abstract.t: This document defines a readiness assessment profile for CNSA 2.0 compliance of TLS deployments. It specifies a structured assessment procedure that evaluates a TLS endpoint's configuration, algorithm selection, and certificate chain against the CNSA 2.0 algorithm requirements, producing a machine-readable readiness report that operators can use to track migration progress and demonstrate compliance.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: CNSA 2.0 establishes the algorithm suite that United States national security systems must use, with transition dates that drive post-quantum adoption. TLS is a primary protocol affected by CNSA 2.0. This document defines a readiness assessment profile: a procedure for evaluating a TLS deployment's compliance with CNSA 2.0 and producing a structured readiness report.
This section will describe the CNSA 2.0 context, the assessment need, and the relationship between this profile and the CyGnScrypt policy framework.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals as shown here.

section.name: Assessment Criteria
section.t: This section will define the assessment criteria: the CNSA 2.0-required TLS cipher suites and key exchange methods, the certificate signature algorithm requirements, and the transition-date constraints. Each criterion will be specified as a machine-checkable rule over the TLS endpoint's negotiated parameters and certificate chain.

section.name: Assessment Procedure
section.t: This section will define the assessment procedure: how an assessor collects the endpoint's TLS configuration (via handshake capture, configuration inspection, and certificate chain retrieval), how each criterion is evaluated, and how the results are aggregated into a readiness report. The procedure will produce a per-criterion pass/fail and an overall readiness status.

section.name: Readiness Report Format
section.t: This section will specify the machine-readable readiness report format: a JSON structure carrying the assessed endpoint identifier, the assessment date, the per-criterion results, the overall status, and references to the CNSA 2.0 requirements that drove any failures. The format will support trend tracking across repeated assessments.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section will address the security of the assessment itself: the integrity of the captured configuration, the risk of assessing a non-representative handshake, and the confidentiality of the readiness report (which reveals endpoint configuration).
